Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor

Class JavaDiagnosticsTools

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.JavaDiagnosticsTools
All Implemented Interfaces:
TextEditorExtension
public final class JavaDiagnosticsTools extends Object implements TextEditorExtension
The bundled "Java Diagnostics" extension: the live half of the Java/Kotlin IDE surface. It compiles the current document with the running JDK's own compiler and reports every problem back to the editor as Diagnostics, which the host paints as gutter dots, wavy underlines and Problems-panel rows (the Phase-0 chrome).

Java is compiled in memory through ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler() with a DiagnosticCollector; the source never touches the disk and class output is dropped into a throwaway directory. Kotlin is analysed by shelling out to kotlinc from PATH and parsing its file:line:col: severity: message output; with no Kotlin install it degrades to an empty result and starts no process.

Analysis runs on a virtual thread and is delivered back on the EDT through a JavaDiagnosticsTools.Scheduler seam; a monotonically increasing generation counter drops a result whenever a newer edit has started, so typing never blocks and stale diagnostics never paint. Every path is headless-testable: the Java compile is synchronous and self-contained, and the scheduler, kotlinc lookup and process runner are injectable seams.
